Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test intent:
  - testNullRecordSeparatorCsv106 builds a CSVFormat with delimiter ';', skipHeaderRecord(true), and a header.
  - It formats values "A", "B" and asserts the result does not end with the literal string "null".
  - The bug report confirms the actual output is "A;Bnull" instead of "A;B".

- Execution path:
  - CSVFormat.format(Object...):
    - Creates a StringWriter and calls new CSVPrinter(out, this).printRecord(values), then returns out.toString().trim().
    - Code: 
      - format: lines 379–387
        - new CSVPrinter(out, this).printRecord(values);
  - CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object...):
    - Iterates values and prints them, then calls println().
    - Code: 
      - printRecord: lines 354–359
        - for (final Object value : values) { print(value); }
        - println();
  - CSVPrinter.println():
    - Fetches the record separator via format.getRecordSeparator() and unconditionally appends it to the writer, then marks a new record.
    - Code:
      - println: lines 323–327
        - final String recordSeparator = format.getRecordSeparator();
        - out.append(recordSeparator);
  - CSVFormat.getRecordSeparator() simply returns the recordSeparator field (lines 486–488), which, by default in CSVFormat.newFormat(char), is null.
    - CSVFormat.newFormat(char) constructs a CSVFormat with recordSeparator = null (lines 261–263).
    - CSVFormat constructor assigns this.recordSeparator = recordSeparator (lines 292–311).

- Why "null" appears:
  - In Java, Writer.append(CharSequence csq) writes the literal string "null" when csq is null.
  - Since CSVFormat.newFormat(';') sets recordSeparator to null and CSVPrinter.println() unconditionally calls out.append(recordSeparator), the StringWriter receives the literal "null".
  - format(...) then returns out.toString().trim(); trim() does not remove "null", so the result ends with "null".

- Root cause:
  - CSVPrinter.println() does not guard against a null recordSeparator. With a null recordSeparator (the default from CSVFormat.newFormat), println() appends the literal "null" to the output, causing outputs like "A;Bnull".
  - withSkipHeaderRecord(true) and withHeader(...) do not affect recordSeparator and are incidental to triggering the default-null behavior.

This explains the failing assertion that the formatted string should not end with "null" and matches the bug report. The fix should ensure that println() does not append anything (or uses a sensible default) when the recordSeparator is null.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
